metadata.name: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS)
metadata.disease_category: Functional gastrointestinal disorder (disorder of gut-brain interaction)
metadata.emergency_level: Routine - but red flags must trigger investigation
metadata.severity: Chronic, non-life-threatening but can be disabling for quality of life

overview.short_description: A common chronic functional bowel disorder of abdominal pain related to defecation with altered bowel habit (diarrhoea, constipation or mixed) and bloating, in the absence of structural disease.
overview.detailed_description: IBS is a positive clinical diagnosis in patients with typical symptoms and no alarm features, supported by limited tests to exclude mimics (notably coeliac disease and, in some, inflammatory bowel disease). It is a disorder of gut-brain interaction. Management is individualised: diet (including low-FODMAP with dietetic support), lifestyle, symptom-directed medication, and psychological therapies. The key safety task is not to miss organic disease signalled by red flags.
overview.pathophysiology: Altered gut-brain signalling, visceral hypersensitivity, dysmotility, changes in gut microbiota/immune activation, and psychosocial factors interact to produce pain and altered bowel habit without structural damage.
overview.etiology: Multifactorial; often post-infectious (after gastroenteritis), with stress/psychological, dietary and microbiome contributions.
overview.natural_history: Chronic and relapsing/remitting; fluctuates with stress and diet; does not progress to serious bowel disease.
overview.prognosis: Good for longevity; symptoms often persist but can be well managed; quality of life impact varies.

prevalence.value: Very common; affects roughly 5-10%+ of adults.

incidence.value: Often begins in early-to-mid adulthood; can follow gastroenteritis.

epidemiology.age_groups: Commonly younger/middle-aged adults; new onset over 50 warrants more caution.

risk_factors.lifestyle: Stress, dietary triggers (certain fermentable carbohydrates/FODMAPs, caffeine, alcohol), irregular eating.
risk_factors.diabetes: Autonomic effects can affect the gut.
risk_factors.family_history: Some familial clustering; coeliac disease in family (differential).
risk_factors.medications: Some drugs alter bowel habit (differential); opioids cause constipation.
risk_factors.previous_diseases: Prior gastroenteritis (post-infectious IBS); anxiety/depression commonly coexist.

chief_complaints.complaint: Recurrent abdominal pain related to bowel movements

symptoms.symptom: Abdominal pain/discomfort related to defecation (relieved or triggered by passing stool)
Mucus per rectum, urgency, incomplete evacuation
Rectal bleeding, weight loss, nocturnal symptoms, or onset >50 (RED FLAGS)
symptoms.importance: RED FLAGS - not IBS; investigate for organic disease

negative_findings.finding: No rectal bleeding, weight loss, anaemia, nocturnal diarrhoea, abdominal/rectal mass, or family history of bowel/ovarian cancer
negative_findings.why_important: Absence of red flags supports a positive IBS diagnosis

negative_findings.finding: Negative coeliac serology and normal inflammatory markers/faecal calprotectin
negative_findings.why_important: Excludes key mimics (coeliac disease, inflammatory bowel disease)

history_questions.question: Is the abdominal pain related to opening your bowels, and has your stool changed in frequency or form?
Any rectal bleeding, weight loss, waking at night with symptoms, or new onset over 50?
Any family history of bowel or ovarian cancer, coeliac disease, or IBD?
Dietary triggers, stress, and impact on daily life?

physical_examination.expected_finding: Usually normal or mild tenderness; a mass is a red flag

physical_examination.examination: Assess for anaemia/weight and (if indicated) rectal examination

vital_signs.bmi: Normal (weight loss is a red flag)

laboratory_tests.indication: Exclude anaemia/inflammation and coeliac disease before diagnosing IBS
laboratory_tests.expected_result: Normal in IBS; positive coeliac serology in coeliac disease

laboratory_tests.indication: Distinguish IBS from inflammatory bowel disease when needed
laboratory_tests.expected_result: Normal/low in IBS; raised in IBD

laboratory_tests.test_name: CA125 (in women with relevant symptoms), stool tests as indicated
laboratory_tests.indication: Exclude ovarian cancer/other causes when features suggest

imaging.when_needed: Only if red flags/atypical features prompt colonoscopy or imaging

other_diagnostic_tests.endoscopy: Colonoscopy only for red flags / to exclude organic disease (not needed for typical IBS)
other_diagnostic_tests.biopsy: As part of colonoscopy/coeliac work-up if indicated
other_diagnostic_tests.culture: Stool culture if infective cause suspected

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: Positive clinical diagnosis (Rome IV): recurrent abdominal pain, on average >=1 day/week in the last 3 months, associated with >=2 of: related to defecation; change in stool frequency; change in stool form. Symptom onset >=6 months earlier, WITHOUT alarm features, and with limited tests excluding mimics (coeliac serology, inflammatory markers/calprotectin). Subtype by predominant stool pattern (IBS-C, IBS-D, IBS-M).
diagnostic_criteria.diagnostic_scores: Rome IV criteria; Bristol stool chart for subtyping.

differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Have you been tested for coeliac disease?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Rectal bleeding, nocturnal symptoms, weight loss, raised calprotectin
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Any blood in stool, weight loss, or waking at night?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Older, weight loss, bleeding, mass, persistent new symptoms
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Any weight loss, bleeding, or new symptoms over age 50?

differential_diagnosis.disease: Bile-acid diarrhoea / other functional or dietary causes
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Is the diarrhoea very watery and does it respond to a bile-acid binder?

diagnostic_questions.question: Any red flags - rectal bleeding, weight loss, anaemia, nocturnal symptoms, mass, or new onset over 50?
diagnostic_questions.purpose: Ensure IBS is a safe positive diagnosis
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: Any red flag -> investigate/refer, do not diagnose IBS

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the pain clearly related to bowel movements with a change in stool pattern?
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: Yes + no red flags + normal basic tests -> IBS

next_best_question.current_situation: Chronic abdominal pain and altered bowel habit
next_best_question.question: Any red flags, and have coeliac serology and calprotectin been checked?
next_best_question.expected_answers: Red flags vs typical IBS with normal tests
next_best_question.branching_logic: Red flags -> investigate/refer; typical + normal tests -> positive IBS diagnosis and management

next_best_test.why: Exclude coeliac disease and IBD before diagnosing IBS

red_flags.finding: Unintentional weight loss or abdominal/rectal mass
Nocturnal diarrhoea/pain or new persistent change in bowel habit over 50
Family history of bowel/ovarian cancer or positive coeliac serology

referral_criteria.urgent_referral: Red flags suggesting cancer (2-week-wait); suspected IBD.
referral_criteria.routine_referral: Diagnostic uncertainty, refractory symptoms, or for dietetic/psychological therapies.
referral_criteria.emergency_referral: Rarely (acute complication of a missed organic diagnosis).

late: Unnecessary investigations if red flags mis-assessed

initial_management.supportive_care: Positive diagnosis and clear explanation/reassurance (a genuine, common condition); address the gut-brain nature and set expectations.
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Antispasmodic; Loperamide; Laxative; Low-dose TCA/selected antidepressant. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_CG61.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Regular meals, adequate hydration, limit caffeine/alcohol/fizzy drinks and trigger foods; a trial of a low-FODMAP diet WITH dietetic support; physical activity; stress management.
initial_management.follow_up: Review response; step up to psychological therapies (CBT/gut-directed hypnotherapy) for refractory symptoms; reassess if new red flags.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: Symptom-directed: antispasmodics for pain; laxatives for IBS-C (avoid lactulose - can worsen bloating; linaclotide for refractory constipation); loperamide for IBS-D; low-dose tricyclic or SSRI antidepressants for pain/global symptoms; consider peppermint oil. Probiotics may help some.

patient_education.home_advice: IBS is a common, genuine condition where the gut is oversensitive, causing pain, bloating and changes in your bowel habit - but it does not damage the bowel or shorten life. Diet changes (regular meals, limiting caffeine/alcohol and certain trigger foods, sometimes a supervised low-FODMAP diet), managing stress, and specific medicines for your main symptom help. See a doctor if you get bleeding from the back passage, lose weight, or your symptoms change - to make sure nothing else is going on.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: القولون العصبي حالة شائعة وحقيقية تكون فيها الأمعاء شديدة الحساسية فتسبّب ألماً وانتفاخاً وتغيّراً في التبرّز - لكنه لا يُتلف الأمعاء ولا يقصّر العمر. تفيد تعديلات الغذاء (وجبات منتظمة، تقليل الكافيين والكحول وبعض الأطعمة المُحفّزة، وأحياناً حِمية منخفضة FODMAP بإشراف)، وإدارة التوتّر، وأدوية موجّهة لعرضك الأساسي. راجع الطبيب إذا ظهر نزيف من الشرج، أو نقص وزنك، أو تغيّرت أعراضك - للتأكد من عدم وجود سبب آخر.
patient_education.prevention: No prevention; trigger management reduces flares.
patient_education.warning_signs: Rectal bleeding, weight loss, waking at night with symptoms, or a new persistent change in bowel habit.

prevention.lifestyle: Trigger and stress management reduce symptom flares.
prevention.screening: Not applicable (age-appropriate bowel cancer screening still applies).

evidence.evidence_level: Moderate-high for dietary, pharmacological and psychological therapies.
evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by NICE_CG61; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.
evidence.legacy_guideline_strength_pre_v13: Strong - NICE CG61, Rome Foundation, BSG.

limitations: Guidelines require individual clinical judgement and may differ by country, formulary and antimicrobial resistance.
The evidence audit verifies traceability and major safety structure; it does not certify every narrative sentence.
No medication should be selected or dosed without patient-specific contraindication and interaction checking.

treatment_guidance.treatment_goal: Use a positive diagnosis and individual symptom-directed treatment after excluding red flags.
treatment_guidance.legacy_narrative_summary: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Antispasmodic; Loperamide; Laxative; Low-dose TCA/selected antidepressant. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_CG61.
required_history_before_any_medication: age and weight where dosing is weight- or age-dependent
pregnancy or breastfeeding status when relevant
documented drug allergies and the exact reaction
all prescribed, OTC, herbal and recreational substances
major cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal and bleeding history
non_drug_measures: Regular meals, activity and soluble fibre; low-FODMAP or exclusion diets only with appropriately trained dietetic guidance.

medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

use_caution_if: glaucoma, urinary retention/prostatic obstruction, constipation, tachyarrhythmia, pregnancy, older/frail patient, or anticholinergic burden
monitoring: symptom response, constipation, urinary retention, vision/cognitive adverse effects
